detail.longDescription: With all the hype around GTA VI, I keep thinking about how we're going to spend hundreds of hours playing these amazing games while sitting on a sofa, barely moving. Sure, you can get a standing desk or a walking treadmill. But wouldn't it be much cooler if the games themselves made you move? There's Wii Sports and fitness games, but they usually have weird graphics and infantile / no stories. I mean proper games, with stories, complex mechanics, interesting worlds, good art. Games you actually want to spend hours playing, except you're moving your body instead of pressing buttons. I've seen people playing games like Elden Ring with dance pads. That's pretty cool, but those games weren't designed for it, so you quickly run into limitations. VR comes somewhat close, but even there you often end up moving around with a joystick. And I'd much rather play on a normal screen, without a headset. With webcams, pose estimation, hand tracking and cheap sensors, it seems like we already have most of the technology. What's missing are the games. I'm making some small experiments myself, but I'd really like to see indie developers take this further. Are there any games like this that I've missed? And if you're developing games, what would stop you from making one?
